name: Exact One-Point-Amalgam Criterion for Dismantlable Ampleness
statement: Let $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ be nonempty ample families on disjoint coordinate blocks, each rooted at $0$, and let $X=A_1\vee\cdots\vee A_m$ be their one-point amalgam. Then $X$ is ample and peels to $0$ exactly when every $A_i$ peels to $0$. Moreover, $X$ is dismantlable ample exactly when every factor is dismantlable ample and at most one factor fails to peel to its root. Hence dismantlable ample classes are not closed under arbitrary one-point amalgams.
proof: No support using coordinates from two exclusive blocks is shattered, so the shadows of the factors meet only at the empty support and the amalgam is ample. A USO of the union restricts to every factor. At the common root, its outgoing directions may lie in at most one exclusive block, because a mixed outgoing square is absent; hence every other factor must have the root as sink. Conversely, choose acyclic USOs rooted at $0$ in all but at most one factor and any acyclic USO in the exceptional factor. Their union satisfies both USO axioms, and a directed cycle cannot pass between pieces through their unique common vertex.
